boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Michigan State University
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food destinations with current late-hours evidence near Michigan State University.

cards.title: Pizza House East Lansing
cards.subtitle: 4790 S. Hagadorn Rd., East Lansing
cards.notes: Use the East Lansing location’s ordering or dining options when you need food later in the evening; confirm service format before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A pizza and Italian-food option with unusually late listed service.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza House lists the East Lansing location and states that dine-in and delivery are available until 4 AM daily.
cards.source_title: Pizza House
cards.access_notes: Official site lists dine-in and delivery until 4 AM daily for Pizza House, 4790 S. Hagadorn, East Lansing.

cards.title: Conrad's Grill II
cards.subtitle: 1219 E. Grand River Ave., East Lansing
cards.notes: Place a pickup or delivery order from the East Lansing shop when its daily late window fits your schedule; check the ordering page for availability.
cards.short_summary: A Grand River food stop with daily hours extending past 2 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Conrad's Grill lists its East Lansing location at 1219 E. Grand River Avenue and daily pickup/delivery hours of 11 AM–2:30 AM.
cards.source_title: Conrad's Grill II — East Lansing
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists daily delivery/pickup hours of 11 AM–2:30 AM.

cards.title: Bell's Greek Pizza
cards.subtitle: 1135 E. Grand River Ave., East Lansing
cards.notes: Plan a Friday or Saturday pizza pickup when the later 1 AM closing applies, and verify holiday or event changes directly with the shop.
cards.short_summary: An East Lansing pizza shop with a later weekend closing time.
cards.evidence_claim: Bell's Greek Pizza lists its East Lansing address and Friday–Saturday hours of 10 AM–1 AM.
cards.source_title: Bell's Greek Pizza
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Friday–Saturday hours through 1 AM; Monday–Thursday and Sunday close at 11 PM.

cards.title: El Azteco East Lansing
cards.subtitle: 225 Ann St., East Lansing
cards.notes: Choose this restaurant for a late meal on Friday or Saturday, when its posted schedule extends to 2 AM; verify conditions before going.
cards.short_summary: A Mexican-food restaurant with a documented 2 AM weekend close.
cards.evidence_claim: El Azteco lists 225 Ann Street in East Lansing and Friday–Saturday operating hours of 11 AM–2 AM.
cards.source_title: El Azteco East Lansing Late Night Menu
cards.access_notes: Official page lists Friday–Saturday hours from 11 AM to 2 AM; Sunday–Thursday close at 11 PM.

cards.title: Denny's East Lansing
cards.subtitle: 2701 E. Grand River Ave., East Lansing
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s location page to check ordering status and choose dine-in, pickup, or delivery as available at the time you need food.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour listed diner option on East Grand River.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny's lists its East Lansing restaurant at 2701 E. Grand River Avenue with store hours of 12 AM–11:58 PM every day.
cards.source_title: Denny's #7908 — East Lansing
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists daily store hours of 12 AM–11:58 PM and supports dine-in, pickup, and delivery.

cards.title: Raising Cane's East Lansing
cards.subtitle: 301 E. Grand River Rd., East Lansing
cards.notes: Use the walk-up window for the documented later Thursday-to-Saturday window; dine-in has an earlier midnight closing every day.
cards.short_summary: A chicken-finger location with a late walk-up window on select nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Raising Cane's lists its 301 E. Grand River Road location’s walk-up window through 2 AM Thursday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Raising Cane's — E Grand River Ave
cards.access_notes: Official page lists walk-up window hours until 2 AM Thursday–Saturday; dine-in hours end at midnight daily.

cards.title: Cottage Inn Pizza East Lansing
cards.subtitle: East Grand River Ave., East Lansing
cards.notes: Order from the East Lansing store within its posted late service window, especially on Friday or Saturday; check the order page for current fulfillment.
cards.short_summary: A pizza option with Friday and Saturday service listed until 2:30 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Cottage Inn Pizza lists East Lansing store hours until 2:30 AM on Friday and Saturday and until 2 AM on Thursday.
cards.source_title: Cottage Inn Pizza East Lansing
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists hours through 2:30 AM Friday–Saturday, 2 AM Thursday, and 1 AM on other days.

cards.entity_name: Taco Bell East Lansing — 7195 E. Saginaw St.
cards.title: Taco Bell on E. Saginaw
cards.subtitle: 7195 E. Saginaw St., East Lansing
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru when its late schedule is active, rather than assuming dining-room availability; consult the location page for day-specific times.
cards.short_summary: A drive-thru option with listed service as late as 4 AM on select nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists the 7195 E. Saginaw Street drive-thru open until 4 AM Thursday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 7195 E. Saginaw St.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru hours until 4 AM Thursday–Saturday, 1:30 AM Monday–Wednesday, and 2 AM Sunday.

cards.title: Shake Shack East Lansing
cards.subtitle: 3106 E. Saginaw St., Lansing
cards.notes: Use the official location page to verify the day’s closing time and select dine-in, delivery, or a listed pickup method before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A burger-and-shake location with midnight daily hours and 1 AM weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Shake Shack lists its East Lansing location at 3106 E. Saginaw Street with hours until midnight daily and until 1 AM Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Shake Shack — East Lansing
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists 10 AM–midnight Sunday–Thursday and 10 AM–1 AM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Crunchy's East Lansing
cards.subtitle: 254 W. Grand River Ave., East Lansing
cards.notes: Consider the restaurant’s food menu during its listed late window, and confirm the date-specific closing time directly before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A West Grand River restaurant with midnight service listed early in the week.
cards.evidence_claim: Crunchy's lists its East Lansing address and Sunday–Wednesday hours from 11 AM until midnight.
cards.source_title: Crunchy's East Lansing — Contact
cards.access_notes: Official contact page lists Sunday–Wednesday hours of 11 AM–12 AM; verify later-week hours directly before visiting.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten distinct MSU places for study, making, art, media, recreation, and outdoor breaks, supported by current official university sources.

cards.title: Walk the Beal Botanical Garden
cards.subtitle: Between the Main Library and IM Circle
cards.notes: Enter through the West Circle Drive gates and take the riverside paths at an unhurried pace; use the free digital guide to identify what you see.
cards.short_summary: A year-round riverside garden for a quiet walk or reset between campus stops.
cards.evidence_claim: Beal Botanical Garden is open to everyone year-round from sunrise to sunset and is always free.
cards.source_title: Visit | Beal Botanical Garden | Michigan State University
cards.access_notes: Open year-round, sunrise to sunset; the garden notes limited entry points for wheelchair and mobility-device users.

cards.entity_name: Eli and Edythe Broad Art Museum at Michigan State University
cards.title: See what is on view at the Broad
cards.subtitle: Campus art museum on Grand River Avenue
cards.notes: Check the exhibition listings before heading over, then give yourself time to move through the galleries and look closely at the current installations.
cards.short_summary: MSU’s contemporary-art museum combines changing exhibitions with a striking campus building.
cards.evidence_claim: The MSU Broad Art Museum identifies itself as the campus art museum, is open Wednesday through Sunday, and states that it is always free.
cards.source_title: MSU Broad Art Museum
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Wednesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; confirm temporary closures and exhibition dates before visiting.

cards.title: Bring a book to People’s Park
cards.subtitle: Between Wells Hall, the International Center, and Erickson Hall
cards.notes: Use the shaded lawn as an outdoor study stop near Wells Hall; pack out what you bring and shift indoors if weather changes.
cards.short_summary: A named lawn and outdoor study area at the center of several academic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU’s virtual tour says People’s Park provides outdoor study space for students and locates it between Wells Hall, the International Center, and Erickson Hall.
cards.source_title: Wells Hall | Virtual tour | Michigan State University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; access and comfort depend on weather and campus conditions.

cards.title: Catch a Campus Center Cinema screening
cards.subtitle: Wells Hall
cards.notes: Look for the cinema’s current schedule, arrive with your MSU student identification, and plan this as a low-key break after classes in Wells Hall.
cards.short_summary: A Wells Hall cinema that screens recently released movies for MSU students.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU’s Wells Hall virtual tour states that the Campus Center Cinema shows recently released movies free to all MSU students.
cards.source_title: Wells Hall | Virtual tour | Michigan State University
cards.access_notes: Free screenings are stated for MSU students; verify the current film schedule and entry requirements before going.

cards.title: Browse the MSU Union Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Room 230, second floor of the MSU Union
cards.notes: Go upstairs from the Abbott Road entrance to view the rotating exhibition, then use the Union’s public spaces for the rest of your campus stop.
cards.short_summary: A small, rotating exhibition gallery embedded in the MSU Union.
cards.evidence_claim: The MSU Union Art Gallery is free and open to the public and hosts rotating exhibitions programmed by MSU’s Department of Art, Art History, and Design.
cards.source_title: MSU Union Art Gallery | Department of Art, Art History, and Design
cards.access_notes: During exhibitions, the gallery lists Monday–Saturday noon–5 p.m.; check for exhibition changes before visiting.

cards.title: Try the Digital Scholarship Lab
cards.subtitle: Main Library, 2 West
cards.notes: Start at the lab desk, ask about available workstations or reservable rooms, and check whether the specialized room you want is already booked.
cards.short_summary: A Main Library lab for digital projects, visualization, VR, and collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Digital Scholarship Lab offers specialized computing, project rooms, a visualization room, a VR room, and reservable spaces in the Main Library.
cards.source_title: FAQ | Digital Scholarship Lab | MSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open to MSU community members and visitors; computers require a campus login, and some spaces require reservation or desk check-in.

cards.title: Plan a project at Hollander Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Main Library, 2 West
cards.notes: Bring a small project idea, review the available fabrication services, and sign in before using the space; ask staff about the right workflow or equipment.
cards.short_summary: A library makerspace designed for hands-on experimentation and cross-disciplinary collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU Libraries describes Hollander Makerspace as an active learning environment and gathering space for collaboration, experimentation, and learning.
cards.source_title: Hollander Makerspace | About | MSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located in the Main Library’s 2 West area; MSU users sign in through single sign-on and other users can create an account for fabrication services.

cards.entity_name: Gerald M. Kline Digital and Multimedia Center
cards.title: Use the Kline Digital & Multimedia Center
cards.subtitle: Main Library, 4 West
cards.notes: Head to the DMC/Vincent Voice Library service desk and ask about media, collaborative technology rooms, or the Media Lab for your class or project.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor library center for media collections, technology, and collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kline Digital and Multimedia Center supports collaborative technology labs, presentation space, media and gaming hardware, and software.
cards.source_title: About the DMC | Gerald M. Kline Digital and Multimedia Center | MSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Access the center from the DMC/Vincent Voice Library service desk on 4 West of the Main Library.

cards.title: Set up a session in the DMC Video Game Labs
cards.subtitle: Gerald M. Kline Digital & Multimedia Center, Main Library 4 West
cards.notes: Check the lab’s reservation and use information, then bring a group or work solo with the available console and PC gaming equipment.
cards.short_summary: Library gaming rooms that support both recreation and academic uses.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU Libraries says the Kline Digital and Multimedia Center’s game labs are available for study and recreation, with console and high-spec PC gaming options.
cards.source_title: Video Game Labs | Gerald M. Kline Digital and Multimedia Center | MSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located in Main Library 4 West; consult the library’s current reservation and equipment-use information before visiting.

cards.title: Explore the Michigan 4-H Children’s Garden
cards.subtitle: MSU Horticulture Gardens, 1066 Bogue Street
cards.notes: Visit during the outdoor season and follow the themed paths through the garden; use the posted map to choose a few areas rather than rushing the whole site.
cards.short_summary: A themed outdoor garden within MSU’s Horticulture Gardens, with nearly 100 named areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Michigan 4-H Children’s Gardens states that there is no admission fee and that its outdoor gardens are open daily from sunup to sundown from April 1 through October 31.
cards.source_title: Information | Michigan 4-H Children's Gardens
cards.access_notes: Outdoor garden season is April 1–October 31, sunup to sundown; parking is separately regulated and may require payment.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten public-facing MSU gardens, galleries, and museum spaces with documented free admission.

cards.title: Walk the W. J. Beal Botanical Garden
cards.subtitle: North campus botanical garden
cards.notes: Meet at the garden entrance, then take an unhurried loop through plant collections and compare what is in bloom before choosing a bench to talk.
cards.short_summary: A year-round botanical-garden walk with no admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU states that the W. J. Beal Botanical Garden is open at all times throughout the year without an admission charge.
cards.source_title: MSU Gardens
cards.access_notes: Open at all times throughout the year; no admission charge, according to MSU.

cards.entity_name: Amien and Florence Center Trial Gardens
cards.title: Browse the Center Trial Gardens
cards.subtitle: MSU Horticulture Gardens
cards.notes: Use the paths to look at the annuals, perennials, and vegetable trials together; pause to pick a few varieties to photograph or sketch.
cards.short_summary: A plant-trial garden for a casual shared walk.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU says the Amien and Florence Center Trial Gardens are open without an admission charge.
cards.source_title: MSU Gardens
cards.access_notes: Part of the MSU Horticulture Gardens; open without an admission charge.

cards.title: Trace the DeLapa Perennial Garden beds
cards.subtitle: MSU Horticulture Gardens
cards.notes: Follow the ten island beds at an easy pace and use the different foliage, bulbs, and grasses as prompts for a low-key conversation or photo walk.
cards.short_summary: A compact perennial garden with ten island beds.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU says the Judith DeLapa Perennial Garden is open without an admission charge.
cards.source_title: MSU Gardens
cards.access_notes: Part of the MSU Horticulture Gardens; open without an admission charge.

cards.title: Explore the MSU 4-H Children's Garden
cards.subtitle: MSU Horticulture Gardens
cards.notes: Bring a friend or younger family member and work through the themed areas together, taking time for the garden's hands-on and interactive features.
cards.short_summary: A themed garden designed for children and the young at heart.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU states that admission to the MSU 4-H Children's Garden is free.
cards.source_title: MSU Gardens
cards.access_notes: MSU identifies more than 56 theme areas and states that admission is free.

cards.title: Take a dawn-to-dusk arboretum walk
cards.subtitle: MSU Horticulture Gardens
cards.notes: Set a route through the arboretum's featured garden areas and specimen trees, then stop at the Japanese or native-plant areas to compare observations.
cards.short_summary: An instructional arboretum with featured garden areas.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU states that the Clarence E. Lewis Landscape Arboretum is open all year, dawn to dusk, with free admission.
cards.source_title: MSU Gardens
cards.access_notes: Open all year from dawn to dusk; admission is free.

cards.entity_name: Kathleen and Milton Muelder Japanese Garden
cards.title: Pause in the Muelder Japanese Garden
cards.subtitle: Within the Clarence E. Lewis Landscape Arboretum
cards.notes: Include this named featured garden on an arboretum walk, slow down at its planted details, and make it a quiet place to catch up with someone.
cards.short_summary: A named Japanese garden within MSU's free arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU identifies the Kathleen and Milton Muelder Japanese Garden as a featured garden area within the Clarence E. Lewis Landscape Arboretum, whose admission is free.
cards.source_title: MSU Gardens
cards.access_notes: Located within the arboretum, which MSU says is open all year, dawn to dusk, with free admission.

cards.entity_name: Yvonne V. Wilson Native Plant Garden
cards.title: Look for native plants at Wilson Garden
cards.subtitle: Within the Clarence E. Lewis Landscape Arboretum
cards.notes: Add this named garden to an arboretum route and take a shared close look at its native plantings; it works well for a short outdoor reset.
cards.short_summary: A named native-plant garden inside MSU's arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU identifies the Yvonne V. Wilson Native Plant Garden as a featured garden area within the Clarence E. Lewis Landscape Arboretum, whose admission is free.
cards.source_title: MSU Gardens
cards.access_notes: Located within the arboretum, which MSU says is open all year, dawn to dusk, with free admission.

cards.title: Sit by the Radiology Healing Gardens
cards.subtitle: MSU Radiology facility grounds
cards.notes: Choose a bench near the gardens, ponds, or waterfalls for a calm conversation, then take a short circuit of the grounds before heading back to campus.
cards.short_summary: Garden grounds with ponds and waterfalls near Radiology.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU states that admission to the Radiology Healing Gardens is free.
cards.source_title: MSU Gardens
cards.access_notes: MSU describes the gardens as a space for visitors, students, and employees; admission is free.

cards.title: Explore the MSU Museum together
cards.subtitle: Museum galleries, East Lansing
cards.notes: Register at the Welcome Center, then move through the exhibitions at your own pace and trade notes on one object or display each person wants to discuss.
cards.short_summary: A free museum visit with self-paced gallery time.
cards.evidence_claim: The MSU Museum states that admission is free for all visitors.
cards.source_title: Visitor Information - MSU Museum
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday through Saturday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; register at the Welcome Center or online.

cards.title: See an exhibition at the Union Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Room 230, MSU Union
cards.notes: Head to the second-floor gallery, view the current exhibition at your own pace, and use one artwork as a starting point for a shared conversation.
cards.short_summary: A public contemporary-art gallery inside the MSU Union.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU states that the MSU Union Art Gallery is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: MSU Union Art Gallery
cards.access_notes: Located at 49 Abbot Road, Room 230; the gallery lists exhibition hours Monday–Saturday, noon–5 p.m.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named MSU Libraries environments for solo work, small-group sessions, and technology-supported collaboration.

cards.entity_name: Main Library First Floor East Wing
cards.title: Main Library First Floor East Wing
cards.subtitle: Main Library · 1st Floor East
cards.notes: Set up for individual work with Mac and Windows computers, MSU Print, electrical outlets, and a designated quiet environment.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, computer-equipped individual-study area.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU Libraries lists this as an individual-study space with computers, printing, outlets, quiet space, and no reservation requirement.
cards.source_title: First Floor, East Wing | MSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: No reservation is required; the listed maximum group size is one.

cards.entity_name: Main Library First Floor West Wing
cards.title: Main Library First Floor West Wing
cards.subtitle: Main Library · 1st Floor West
cards.notes: Use the individual-study seating when you need Windows computers, nearby electrical outlets, and room for a small work session.
cards.short_summary: An individual-study area with Windows computers and outlets.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU Libraries identifies this as individual study seating for up to four, with Windows computers, electrical outlets, and no reservation requirement.
cards.source_title: First Floor, West Wing | MSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: No reservation is required; MSU Libraries lists a maximum group size of four.

cards.title: Main Library South Lobby
cards.subtitle: Main Library · Main Floor Center
cards.notes: Bring a charged device and use the lobby’s listed electrical outlets for an individual session or a small four-person work block.
cards.short_summary: A central first-floor study setting with power access.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU Libraries lists the South Lobby as an individual-study space with electrical outlets, seating for 62, and no reservation requirement.
cards.source_title: South Lobby, First Floor | MSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: No reservation is required; the listed maximum group size is four.

cards.entity_name: Main Library First Floor Meeting Room E102
cards.title: First Floor Meeting Room E102
cards.subtitle: Main Library · 1st Floor East
cards.notes: Reserve this room for a focused project meeting when a Smart Board, video projector, Windows computer, and quiet setting help.
cards.short_summary: A reservable, technology-equipped group room for up to ten.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU Libraries lists E102 as a reservable group-study and meeting room for up to 10 with a Smart Board and video projector.
cards.source_title: First Floor Meeting Room - E102 | MSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reserve online and check in at the Circulation Desk on 1-Center.

cards.entity_name: Second Floor West Study Rooms W208–W213 and W218–W219
cards.title: Second Floor West Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Main Library · 2nd Floor West
cards.notes: Choose one of these rooms for quiet individual or group work; each listed room has a chalkboard and seats up to eight.
cards.short_summary: First-come rooms combining quiet space with chalkboards.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU Libraries lists these rooms as quiet individual and group study spaces for up to eight, with chalkboards and no reservation requirement.
cards.source_title: Second Floor West Study Rooms W208-W213, W218-W219 | MSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: No reservation is required; the listed seating capacity and maximum group size are eight.

cards.entity_name: Third Floor West Study Rooms W309–W313 and W317–W320
cards.title: Third Floor West Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Main Library · 3rd Floor West
cards.notes: Use these quiet rooms for individual or group work when a whiteboard, markers, eraser, and an eight-person capacity are useful.
cards.short_summary: First-come quiet study rooms with whiteboard tools.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU Libraries lists these rooms as quiet individual and group study spaces for up to eight, with whiteboards and no reservation requirement.
cards.source_title: Third Floor West Study Rooms W309-W313, W317-W320 | MSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: No reservation is required; MSU Libraries lists seating for up to eight.

cards.entity_name: Main Library East Wing Quiet Study Space
cards.title: Main Library East Wing Quiet Study Space
cards.subtitle: Main Library · East Wing
cards.notes: Head to the designated quiet-study wing when you need a low-noise reading or writing setting instead of a conversational work room.
cards.short_summary: A library wing formally designated for quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU Libraries states that the entire East wing of the Main Library is designated as quiet study space.
cards.source_title: Main Library Building Accessibility & Equipment | MSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Use the Main Library during its posted building-access hours; no separate reservation rule is listed for the wing.

cards.entity_name: Gast Business Library Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Gast Business Library Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Gast Business Library · Rooms 25, 26, 27, 30, 31, 32 and 35
cards.notes: Reserve a room for a group project with a large monitor, wireless conferencing kit, whiteboard, and dry-erase markers available for checkout.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group rooms with display and videoconference tools.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU Libraries lists seven Gast Business Library group study rooms with monitors, Cisco Mini Room Kits, whiteboards, and a 10-person maximum.
cards.source_title: Group Study & Tech Spaces | Business Library | MSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: MSU-affiliated users with current MSU ID reserve and check in at the Business Library Circulation Desk; maximum time is two hours.

cards.entity_name: Gast Business Library Group Study Alcoves
cards.title: Gast Business Library Group Study Alcoves
cards.subtitle: Gast Business Library · Alcoves A, B, C and D
cards.notes: Reserve an open alcove for a project team that needs a large monitor, wireless conferencing kit, whiteboard, and space for up to eight.
cards.short_summary: Open reservable alcoves for small-group work and web conferences.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU Libraries lists four open group-study alcoves with monitors, Cisco Mini Room Kits, whiteboards, and an eight-person maximum.
cards.source_title: Group Study & Tech Spaces | Business Library | MSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: MSU ID is required to reserve and check in at the Business Library Circulation Desk; reservations are limited to two consecutive hours.

cards.entity_name: Gast Business Library Collaborative Technology Lab
cards.title: Gast Business Library Collaborative Technology Lab
cards.subtitle: Gast Business Library · Room 13
cards.notes: Reserve Room 13 for a larger collaborative session using its monitors, wireless conferencing kit, whiteboards, movable tables, and wheeled chairs.
cards.short_summary: A reservable technology lab for collaborative work of up to 15.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU Libraries lists the Gast Business Library Collaborative Technology Lab in Room 13 with conferencing technology, whiteboards, movable furniture, and a 15-person maximum.
cards.source_title: Group Study & Tech Spaces | Business Library | MSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reserve with an MSU ID and check in at the Business Library Circulation Desk; Broad College and HRLR users receive priority.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along the Grand River, Albert Avenue, Abbot Road, and Charles Street corridors beside Michigan State University.

cards.entity_name: Eli and Edythe Broad Art Museum
cards.title: Grand River Avenue: Broad Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Grand River Avenue corridor, at the campus edge
cards.notes: Walk the Grand River frontage to view the angular building, then use the museum’s visit page to plan a gallery stop and accessible arrival.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary-art stop built directly into the campus-to-downtown edge.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum identifies its site as between Grand River Avenue and East Circle Drive, near Farm Lane.
cards.source_title: About the MSU Broad Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Check the museum visit page for current gallery access and parking details.

cards.title: Charles Street: Metrospace exhibitions
cards.subtitle: Charles Street, just off the Grand River Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition listing before heading to Charles Street; the space presents visual-art shows and nontraditional performances in downtown East Lansing.
cards.short_summary: A university-operated downtown gallery and performance space.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU describes (SCENE) Metrospace as an exhibition and non-traditional performance space just off Grand River Avenue on Charles Street.
cards.source_title: (SCENE) Metrospace
cards.access_notes: The official page lists current public hours; confirm them before visiting.

cards.title: West Circle Drive: MSU Museum
cards.subtitle: West Circle Drive, one block from Grand River Avenue
cards.notes: Use the museum’s directions page to pair a West Circle Drive visit with Beaumont Tower and the Main Library area; visitor parking guidance is provided.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum stop immediately north of the Main Library.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU Museum states that it is at 409 West Circle Drive, immediately east of Beaumont Tower and north of the Main Library.
cards.source_title: MSU Museum Maps, Directions and Parking
cards.access_notes: The official directions page identifies Grand River Avenue Ramp 6 as suggested visitor parking.

cards.title: Abbot Road: East Lansing Public Library
cards.subtitle: Abbot Road corridor, north of campus
cards.notes: Use the library’s official calendar or catalog before going, and include its outdoor mural in a self-guided public-art walk along Abbot Road.
cards.short_summary: A civic library and public-art waypoint close to downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of East Lansing lists the East Lansing Public Library among local arts venues and identifies an East Lansing Public Library mural in its public-art resources.
cards.source_title: City of East Lansing Arts
cards.access_notes: Confirm library entry and program availability on its official website before visiting.

cards.title: Grand River Avenue: Curious Book Shop
cards.subtitle: Grand River Avenue corridor, downtown East Lansing
cards.notes: Browse the shop’s current stock and events online first, then make this a book-focused stop while walking the downtown stretch of Grand River Avenue.
cards.short_summary: An independently named bookshop on the downtown corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of East Lansing includes Curious Book Shop in its downtown shopping resources.
cards.source_title: City of East Lansing Resource Directory
cards.access_notes: Verify current retail hours directly with the shop.

cards.title: Grand River Avenue: Rocket Fizz
cards.subtitle: Grand River Avenue corridor, downtown East Lansing
cards.notes: Use this stop for a packaged-soda and candy browse; check the storefront’s current listing before walking over from the campus edge.
cards.short_summary: A named soda-pop and candy shop on Grand River Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: A City of East Lansing downtown newsletter identifies Rocket Fizz as a soda pop and candy shop at 217 East Grand River Avenue.
cards.source_title: City of East Lansing Spring 2024 Newsletter
cards.access_notes: Confirm current storefront hours before visiting.

cards.title: Grand River Avenue: Moka & Co.
cards.subtitle: Grand River Avenue corridor at Bailey Street
cards.notes: Plan a coffee or pastry stop at the Grand River and Bailey corner; verify the current menu and service details on the business’s official channels.
cards.short_summary: A named coffee shop at a documented downtown corner.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of East Lansing’s downtown newsletter identifies Moka & Co. as a Yemeni coffee shop at the corner of Grand River Avenue and Bailey Street.
cards.source_title: City of East Lansing Spring 2024 Newsletter
cards.access_notes: Confirm current service hours directly with the business.

cards.title: Grand River Avenue: Bowl Above
cards.subtitle: Grand River Avenue corridor, east of Bailey Street
cards.notes: Check the official venue page for lane availability and group details, then schedule a bowling activity along the east end of the Grand River corridor.
cards.short_summary: A named bowling destination on the campus-adjacent avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of East Lansing Resource Directory lists Bowl Above at 1001 East Grand River Avenue and links to its official website.
cards.source_title: City of East Lansing Resource Directory
cards.access_notes: Reserve or confirm availability with the venue before visiting.

cards.title: Albert Avenue: Barrio Tacos
cards.subtitle: Albert Avenue corridor, downtown East Lansing
cards.notes: Use the location page to confirm the East Lansing restaurant and current menu, then make Albert Avenue the route for a meal stop.
cards.short_summary: A named restaurant location on Albert Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of East Lansing Resource Directory lists Barrio Tacos at 202 Albert Avenue and links to its East Lansing location page.
cards.source_title: City of East Lansing Resource Directory
cards.access_notes: Confirm current dining availability and service details directly with the restaurant.

cards.title: Albert Avenue: Dave’s Hot Chicken
cards.subtitle: Albert Avenue corridor, downtown East Lansing
cards.notes: Check the restaurant’s current East Lansing location information before walking the Albert Avenue corridor for a casual food stop.
cards.short_summary: A named chicken restaurant documented on Albert Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of East Lansing’s downtown newsletter states that Dave’s Hot Chicken had opened for business on Albert Avenue.
cards.source_title: City of East Lansing Spring 2024 Newsletter
cards.access_notes: Confirm current location hours and menu directly with the restaurant.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented Michigan State rituals, events, songs, and student-section practices.

cards.title: Add a Message to The Rock
cards.subtitle: Outside the MSU Auditorium
cards.notes: Plan a group message or artwork for the painted landmark, then respect the next group’s turn to refresh this evolving campus billboard.
cards.short_summary: Students repeatedly repaint a class gift from 1873 with messages, art, and announcements.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU describes painting The Rock as a campus tradition; the rock was a gift from the Class of 1873 and now functions as a painted student billboard.
cards.source_title: Campus tradition: Painting the Rock
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark outside the MSU Auditorium; follow current university policies.

cards.title: Join the Izzone Student Section
cards.subtitle: Breslin Student Events Center
cards.notes: Check current student-ticket and membership details before a game, then participate from the designated basketball student section.
cards.short_summary: MSU basketball’s student section, named for coach Tom Izzo, began in 1995.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU calls the Izzone a defining tradition of Michigan State basketball and says it began in 1995 with 180 students.
cards.source_title: For 30 years, Izzone is a defining tradition of MSU basketball
cards.access_notes: Game admission, student eligibility, and membership requirements vary by season.

cards.title: Follow the Izzone Campout
cards.subtitle: Munn Field, Michigan State University
cards.notes: Use official Izzone announcements for the current schedule and rules; participants check in and remain within the designated field.
cards.short_summary: A basketball-season campout connected to Izzone lower-bowl standing.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU documents the Izzone Campout as a student tradition first held in 1996 on Munn Field, with check-ins for participants.
cards.source_title: MSU Traditions: A Field of Green and White Tents
cards.access_notes: Only participate if MSU and Izzone organizers announce a current, supervised campout.

cards.title: Hear About the Midnight Scream
cards.subtitle: Michigan State University campus
cards.notes: Treat it as a documented student tradition rather than an instruction to disrupt others; follow quiet-hours and university conduct rules.
cards.short_summary: A newer Spartan tradition associated with finals-week student culture.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU’s 2026 student-traditions exhibition identifies the midnight scream during finals week as a newer Spartan tradition.
cards.source_title: From the Shadows of Beaumont Tower: Hands-On Curatorial Experience Brings Spartan Traditions to Life
cards.access_notes: Observe all residence-hall, quiet-hours, and university conduct policies.

cards.title: Return the Call: “Go White!”
cards.subtitle: Michigan State University community
cards.notes: When someone offers “Go Green,” answer “Go White” in an appropriate public setting and keep the exchange welcoming and respectful.
cards.short_summary: A call-and-response expression of Spartan spirit used by the campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: An MSU student reflection identifies shouting “Go Green” and hearing “Go White” in return as part of the Spartan experience.
cards.source_title: Student view: How MSU traditions, culture shaped my Spartan experience
cards.access_notes: An informal, all-ages expression; use considerate volume and context.

cards.title: Learn the Fight Song
cards.subtitle: Michigan State athletic events
cards.notes: Use MSU’s published materials to learn “Victory for MSU,” then sing along at an official event if you choose to attend.
cards.short_summary: The official fight song is a recurring part of Spartan sporting events.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU states that “Victory for MSU” is an official university song and that the fight song is played at Spartan sporting events.
cards.source_title: Join the Global Spartan Network
cards.access_notes: Event entry and seating requirements depend on the specific sporting event.

cards.title: Watch the Kickstep Entrance
cards.subtitle: Spartan Stadium
cards.notes: Arrive through the proper game entry before pregame to watch the band’s rapid, choreographed stadium entrance from an authorized seat.
cards.short_summary: The Spartan Marching Band’s distinctive kickstep accompanies its stadium entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU documents the Spartan Marching Band’s kickstep as a distinctive routine used when the band makes its stadium entrance.
cards.source_title: MSU Traditions: The Spartan Marching Band
cards.access_notes: Visible during applicable football pregame programming; game admission is generally required.

cards.title: Listen for “MSU Shadows”
cards.subtitle: Beaumont Tower and Spartan sporting events
cards.notes: Listen for the alma mater at the tower or an official game, and use the published song materials if you want to recognize it.
cards.short_summary: MSU Shadows is the university’s official alma mater and is automated daily at Beaumont Tower.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU identifies MSU Shadows as an official university song and reports that Beaumont Tower is automated to play it every day.
cards.source_title: Celebrating Beaumont Tower's 93rd birthday
cards.access_notes: Outdoor listening near Beaumont Tower is generally possible; follow campus access guidance.

cards.title: Know the Beaumont Tower Legend
cards.subtitle: Beaumont Tower courtyard
cards.notes: Visit the tower courtyard and read the legend as campus folklore; participation is entirely optional and should always be consensual.
cards.short_summary: Campus lore says a midnight kiss in Beaumont Tower’s shadow predicts a lasting relationship.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU’s virtual tour records the campus legend that a couple kissing in Beaumont Tower’s shadow, or courtyard at midnight, will stay together forever.
cards.source_title: Beaumont Tower
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; this is folklore, not a required activity. Respect consent and campus policies.

cards.title: Start the Year at Sparticipation
cards.subtitle: IM East Field, Michigan State University
cards.notes: Visit the annual involvement fair to meet registered student organizations, departments, and community participants before choosing where to get involved.
cards.short_summary: A large annual fair that launches the academic year’s student-organization involvement.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU describes Sparticipation as a free annual involvement fair connecting students with organizations, departments, and the broader community.
cards.source_title: Sparticipation
cards.access_notes: The official page lists Sparticipation 2026 for August 30 at IM East Field, 1–5 p.m. ET.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Michigan State University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A daylight-to-evening first-weekend route through campus landmarks, public collections, a student hub, and East Lansing’s Sunday market.

cards.title: Start at the MSU Union
cards.subtitle: North Neighborhood gathering point
cards.notes: Use the Union as a practical first stop: orient yourself in its study spaces, then check its listed dining, shopping, and activity resources.
cards.short_summary: A campus hub with student resources and gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU says the Union has study spaces, computer labs, meeting rooms, shopping, dining, entertainment, and student-support offices.
cards.source_title: About | MSU Union
cards.access_notes: Check the Union’s building-hours page before arriving; individual services may have separate access or purchase requirements.

cards.title: Photograph Bronze Sparty
cards.subtitle: Inside the MSU Union
cards.notes: Pause for a group photo with Bronze Sparty while you are in the Union, then continue toward the campus highlights around West Circle Drive.
cards.short_summary: A named statue stop inside the student union.
cards.evidence_claim: The MSU Union directs visitors not to miss a photo with Bronze Sparty.
cards.source_title: About | MSU Union
cards.access_notes: Located in the MSU Union; confirm building access and hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Eli and Edythe Broad Art Museum
cards.title: Step into the Broad Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Contemporary art at the campus edge
cards.notes: Walk through the galleries and spend time with one or two works that catch your attention; the museum’s current exhibitions rotate.
cards.short_summary: Free contemporary-art galleries in Zaha Hadid’s landmark building.
cards.evidence_claim: The MSU Broad Art Museum says it is always free and open to all, with more than 20,000 square feet of gallery space.
cards.source_title: About - MSU Broad Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Current listed hours are Wednesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; check closure notices and exhibition details before visiting.

cards.title: Hear Beaumont Tower
cards.subtitle: Old campus, near the Red Cedar bicycle trail
cards.notes: Walk by the tower and, if your weekend aligns with a posted recital, listen from the lawn rather than relying on tower access.
cards.short_summary: MSU’s 49-bell carillon anchors old campus.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU identifies Beaumont Tower’s 49-bell carillon and lists Wednesday noon recitals during the school year.
cards.source_title: Beaumont Tower Carillon | Experience MSU
cards.access_notes: The tower’s public climb is generally tied to the first Wednesday noon recital; it has 73 steps and no elevator or restroom.

cards.title: Browse the MSU Museum
cards.subtitle: 409 W. Circle Drive
cards.notes: Register at the Welcome Center, then choose an exhibit to explore at your own pace; allow time to use the museum’s digital guide.
cards.short_summary: Free museum galleries beside Beaumont Tower.
cards.evidence_claim: The MSU Museum states that admission is free for all visitors and that it is open Tuesday through Saturday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Visitor Information - MSU Museum
cards.access_notes: Register in person at the Welcome Center or online; visit Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m., subject to posted closures.

cards.title: Settle into the Main Library
cards.subtitle: 366 W. Circle Drive
cards.notes: Find a study seat, browse the stacks, or use the building as a reset point before the next stop; check the live schedule first.
cards.short_summary: A public-access library and study stop on West Circle Drive.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU Libraries allows any individual free access to its facilities, stack collections, space, and resources.
cards.source_title: Public Access | Library Policies | MSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Hours vary. Between 10 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. Sunday–Thursday, students, staff, and faculty must scan an MSU ID to enter.

cards.title: Walk the Beal Botanical Garden
cards.subtitle: Campus garden and arboretum
cards.notes: Take a slow loop through the named garden and use the plant labels as prompts for conversation; stay on designated paths and respect plantings.
cards.short_summary: A campus garden focused on people, plants, and place.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU says the Beal Botanical Garden and Campus Arboretum supports learning, research, and stewardship around people, plants, and place.
cards.source_title: Beal Botanical Garden | Michigan State University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and programming can change; consult the garden’s official site before visiting.

cards.title: Visit the MSU Dairy Store
cards.subtitle: Anthony Hall, 474 S. Shaw Lane
cards.notes: Choose a snack or simply visit during open hours, then look for the self-guided dairy-plant observation experience described by MSU.
cards.short_summary: A campus dairy store with a self-guided observation deck.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU describes a self-guided Dairy Foods Complex observation-deck tour about milk, cheese, and ice-cream processing.
cards.source_title: MSU Dairy Store | Experience MSU
cards.access_notes: The store lists Tuesday–Sunday, noon–9 p.m.; it is cashless and the weekend entrance is via the back patio doors in Lot 43.

cards.title: Check out IM East
cards.subtitle: 804 E. Shaw Lane, east campus
cards.notes: If you have the required access, use the facility for a casual indoor activity; otherwise, use the exterior as a waypoint on the east-campus walk.
cards.short_summary: An east-campus recreation facility with courts, track, and fitness space.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU lists IM East’s indoor gym areas, racquetball and squash courts, volleyball courts, indoor track, and fitness room.
cards.source_title: IM East | Recreational Sports and Fitness Services | Michigan State University
cards.access_notes: IM East is membership-only; an MSU ID or Rec Sports access card is required, and guests and children are not permitted.

cards.title: Close at the East Lansing Farmers Market
cards.subtitle: Valley Court Park, 280 Valley Court
cards.notes: On a Sunday market day, walk the vendor stalls, read the weekly shopping checklist, and buy only what you want to carry home.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal, growers-only market steps from campus and downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of East Lansing says its growers-only market runs Sundays, June 7–October 25, 2026, from 10 a.m.–2 p.m. at Valley Court Park.
cards.source_title: Farmers Market | East Lansing, MI - Official Website
cards.access_notes: Seasonal Sunday market: June 7–October 25, 2026, 10 a.m.–2 p.m. at Valley Court Park; purchases are optional but vendor goods cost money.
